title: A Russian Assassin Tells His Story

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在 11 月 18 日在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily, today.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》，今天的内容是。

sentences.en: Under President Vladimir Putin, Russia has carried out a brazen campaign of state-sponsored assassinations.
sentences.zh: 在弗拉基米尔·普京总统的领导下，俄罗斯实施了一场肆无忌惮的国营暗杀行动。

sentences.en: My colleague Michael Schwartz tracked down one of the assassins behind that campaign.
sentences.zh: 我的同事迈克尔·施瓦茨追踪了这场行动背后的其中一名刺客。

sentences.en: It's Monday, April 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 4 月 8 日，星期一。

sentences.en: So there's this small town in western Ukraine called Rivna.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰西部有一个叫里夫纳的小镇。

sentences.en: It's old.
sentences.zh: 它很古老。

sentences.en: It has a number of Orthodox Christian cathedrals and a good theater.
sentences.zh: 那里有许多东正教大教堂和一个不错的剧院。

sentences.en: And there's a man named Oleg Smarodinov who moves into this small town.
sentences.zh: 有一个名叫奥列格·斯马罗迪诺夫的男人搬进了这个小镇。

sentences.en: He rents an apartment on the first floor of an old Soviet-style building.
sentences.zh: 他在一栋苏联时期老建筑的一楼租了一套公寓。

sentences.en: But he's not there because he wants to live in this apartment.
sentences.zh: 但他来这里不是因为他想住在这套公寓里。

sentences.en: He's there because he wants to keep an eye on someone.
sentences.zh: 他来这里是因为他想监视某个人。

sentences.en: A man who lives on the sixth floor of the same building.
sentences.zh: 一个住在同一栋楼六楼的男人。

sentences.en: That man was on a list of six people that Oleg had been given by two handlers who had sent him to this town.
sentences.zh: 那个男人在奥列格派来的两个上级给他的六人名单上。

sentences.en: Describe this liSt.
sentences.zh: 描述一下这份名单。

sentences.en: There were six names on the list, each with addresses and dates of birth.
sentences.zh: 名单上有六个名字，每个名字都有地址和出生日期。

sentences.en: And each of the names on the list was given a code name, the name of a flower in Russian.
sentences.zh: 名单上的每个名字都被赋予了一个代号，即俄语中一种花的名字。

sentences.en: So there was Lütik, which is buttercup.
sentences.zh: 所以有柳蒂克，也就是毛茛。

sentences.en: There was Szipovnik, which is briar.
sentences.zh: 还有希波夫尼克，也就是野玫瑰。

sentences.en: And the name of the man on the sixth floor that Oleg was watching was Ivan Mamchur.
sentences.zh: 奥列格监视的六楼男人的名字叫伊万·马姆丘尔。

sentences.en: And his code name was Rosa, or the Rose.
sentences.zh: 他的代号是罗萨，也就是玫瑰。

sentences.en: And what did Oleg know about this man, the Rose?
sentences.zh: 奥列格对这个叫“玫瑰”的男人了解多少？

sentences.en: What does he learn by watching him?
sentences.zh: 他通过监视了解到了什么？

sentences.en: Oleg knows very little initially about this man.
sentences.zh: 奥列格最初对这个男人知之甚少。

sentences.en: He learns that he's a man who keeps the routine.
sentences.zh: 他了解到这是一个生活有规律的人。

sentences.en: He leaves every morning at around 6.30, 7 o'clock, takes his bicycle, goes to work.
sentences.zh: 他每天早上六点半到七点左右离开，骑着自行车去上班。

sentences.en: He works as an electrician at a local jail.
sentences.zh: 他在当地监狱当电工。

sentences.en: He comes back around 6 o'clock in the evening, goes into his apartment, and really doesn't come out all that much.
sentences.zh: 他晚上六点左右回来，进自己的公寓，基本上不太出门。

sentences.en: He certainly doesn't know why he's there to watch him.
sentences.zh: 他当然不知道自己为什么要来监视他。

sentences.en: His handlers were vague, but what they did tell him was that this was an enemy.
sentences.zh: 他的上级说得很模糊，但他们确实告诉他这是一个敌人。

sentences.en: This was somebody that had done something bad in his paSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个过去做过坏事的人。

sentences.en: And so what happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: Oleg watches Ivan for about a month and a half.
sentences.zh: 奥列格监视了伊万大约一个半月。

sentences.en: And then one day, he gets a text message written in Russian.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，他收到一条用俄语写的短信。

sentences.en: It's cryptic, but he knows what it means.
sentences.zh: 它含糊不清，但他知道这意味着什么。

sentences.en: It says,
sentences.zh: 上面写着，

sentences.en: Which means,
sentences.zh: 意思是，

sentences.en: At that point, Oleg positions himself on the sixth floor in the hallway outside of Ivan's apartment and waits for him to come home.
sentences.zh: 在那时，奥列格将自己定位在伊万公寓外面六楼的走廊里，等待他回家。

sentences.en: He stands there, I'm not exactly sure for how long, smoking cigarettes with a gun in his hand, a silenced pistol.
sentences.zh: 他站在那里，我不确定具体多久，手里拿着一把装有消音器的枪抽着烟。

sentences.en: And when the elevator doors open, he calls Ivan's name.
sentences.zh: 当电梯门打开时，他叫了伊万的名字。

sentences.en: Ivan turns to him, and Oleg opens fire.
sentences.zh: 伊万转向他，奥列格开枪了。

sentences.en: He shoots him eight times.
sentences.zh: 他向他开枪八次。

sentences.en: But instead of falling to the ground immediately, Ivan turns and walks towards Oleg and says, in Russian,
sentences.zh: 但伊万没有立即倒地，而是转身走向奥列格，用俄语说道：

sentences.en: Which means,
sentences.zh: 意思是，

sentences.en: It's not me.
sentences.zh: 不是我。

sentences.en: I'm not guilty.
sentences.zh: 我是无辜的。

sentences.en: And then he falls dead to the floor.
sentences.zh: 然后他倒在地上死了。

sentences.en: And Michael, how do you know all of these intimate details of this murder?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，你是怎么知道这起谋杀案的所有这些详细细节的？

sentences.en: I came to this story by reporting on another attempted Russian assassination, the poisoning of Sergei Skripal.
sentences.zh: 我是通过报道另一起俄罗斯未遂暗杀事件——谢尔盖·斯克里帕尔中毒案，才接触到这个故事的。

sentences.en: Police worked well into the night, carefully examining the site of a bizarre incident they still can't explain.
sentences.zh: 警察工作到深夜，仔细检查了一起他们仍然无法解释的离奇事件的现场。

sentences.en: It happened yesterday in a shopping area.
sentences.zh: 它昨天发生在购物区。

sentences.en: In March last year, British authorities found Mr. Skripal and his daughter twitching and unresponsive on a bench.
sentences.zh: 去年三月，英国当局发现斯克里帕尔先生和他的女儿在长椅上抽搐且毫无反应。

sentences.en: There was a couple, an older guy and a younger girl.
sentences.zh: 有一对夫妇，一个老年男子和一个年轻女孩。

sentences.en: She was sort of lent in on him.
sentences.zh: 她有点靠在他身上。

sentences.en: It looked like she'd passed out, maybe.
sentences.zh: 看起来她可能晕倒了。

sentences.en: Actually initially thought that they were suffering from a drug overdose.
sentences.zh: 其实最初以为他们是药物过量。

sentences.en: He was doing some strange hand movements, looking up to the sky.
sentences.zh: 他做了一些奇怪的手势，抬头看着天空。

sentences.en: But they very quickly realized that they had been poisoned.
sentences.zh: 但他们很快意识到他们中毒了。

sentences.en: In a statement released in the past hour or so, police said the pair came into contact with a nerve agent, furthermore.
sentences.zh: 警察在大约过去一个小时左右发布的声明中表示，两人接触了一种神经毒剂，此外。

sentences.en: They both remained critically ill.
sentences.zh: 两人均处于危重状态。

sentences.en: As the investigation delved deeper, they determined that, in fact, Mr. Skripal was a former Russian spy.
sentences.zh: 随着调查的深入，他们确定斯克里帕尔先生实际上前俄罗斯间谍。

sentences.en: And that he had been poisoned by agents sent by the Kremlin to kill him.
sentences.zh: 并且他被克里姆林宫派出的特工毒害以杀死他。

sentences.en: Leaving him twitching on his bench.
sentences.zh: 留下他在长椅上抽搐。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The government has concluded that it is highly likely that Russia was responsible for the act against Sergei and Yulia Skripal.
sentences.zh: 政府得出结论，极有可能是俄罗斯对谢尔盖和尤利娅·斯克里帕尔采取了行动。

sentences.en: This sets off a geopolitical conflict between the West and Russia.
sentences.zh: 这引发了西方与俄罗斯之间的地缘政治冲突。

sentences.en: Alone, Russia's crime is worthy of this council's action.
sentences.zh: 仅凭俄罗斯的罪行，就值得采取安理会行动。

sentences.en: But this is not an isolated incident.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是孤立事件。

sentences.en: The US is removing 60 Russian officials.
sentences.zh: 美国正在驱逐 60 名俄罗斯官员。

sentences.en: An entire consulate will be closed.
sentences.zh: 整个领事馆将被关闭。

sentences.en: Chancellor Merkel and President Macron agreed that there is no plausible explanation other than that the Russian state was responsible.
sentences.zh: 默克尔总理和马克龙总统一致认为，除了俄罗斯国家负有责任外，没有其他合理的解释。

sentences.en: It's now 16 EU nations following suit.
sentences.zh: 现在有 16 个欧盟国家效仿。

sentences.en: One by one, they joined Britain in a standoff with the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 他们一个接一个地加入英国，与克里姆林宫对峙。

sentences.en: What was most frustrating for me as a reporter about the Skripal case was that there was very little I could find out about the mechanism by which these sorts of attacks were carried out.
sentences.zh: 作为一名记者，关于斯克里帕尔案最让我沮丧的是，我很难查明这类袭击事件的实施机制。

sentences.en: When these sorts of things happen, we are reliant on Western intelligence services, if they give us anything.
sentences.zh: 当发生这类事情时，如果西方情报机构给我们提供任何信息，我们就依赖他们。

sentences.en: We're reliant on Western law enforcement services.
sentences.zh: 我们依赖西方的执法部门。

sentences.en: Normally, you get nothing but denials from the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，你从克里姆林宫得到的只是否认。

sentences.en: And what I was looking for is for somebody to explain to me how these assassinations,
sentences.zh: 而我一直在寻找的是有人向我解释这些暗杀是如何进行的，

sentences.en: how these operations are carried out from the point of view of the people who are plotting them.
sentences.zh: 从策划者的角度来看，这些行动是如何进行的。

sentences.en: You wanted to know from the other side how this all works.
sentences.zh: 你想从另一方了解这一切是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: And so I went looking for cases that could help better explain how these sorts of assassinations and assassination attempts are carried out.
sentences.zh: 所以我去寻找能够更好地解释这类暗杀和暗杀未遂是如何进行的案例。

sentences.en: And that brought me to Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这把我带到了乌克兰。

sentences.en: And why Ukraine?
sentences.zh: 为什么是乌克兰？

sentences.en: A steady stream of anti-Kremlin figures have been assassinated on Kiev's streets.
sentences.zh: 源源不断的反克里姆林宫人物在基辅街头被暗杀。

sentences.en: Mostly because there have been a number of assassinations in recent years, a lot of them attributed to Russia.
sentences.zh: 主要是因为近年来发生了一系列暗杀事件，其中很多被归咎于俄罗斯。

sentences.en: A former Russian lawmaker who defected to Ukraine in 2016 was shot dead outside a hotel in Kiev.
sentences.zh: 2016年叛逃到乌克兰的前俄罗斯议员在基辅一家酒店外被枪杀。

sentences.en: The surveillance video appearing to show the assassination of a vocal critic of Russian President Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 监控视频似乎显示了对俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京直言不讳的批评者的暗杀。

sentences.en: The blast comes nearly a year after investigative journalist Pavel Sheremet was killed in a car bomb.
sentences.zh: 这次爆炸发生在调查记者帕维尔·舍列梅特在汽车炸弹中丧生近一年后。

sentences.en: It marked another dark moment in the awful relationship between Russia and Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这标志着俄罗斯与乌克兰糟糕关系中的又一个黑暗时刻。

sentences.en: And so I talked to a source who had some knowledge about some of these cases.
sentences.zh: 所以我采访了一个对其中一些案例有所了解的消息人士。

sentences.en: And one of the cases he mentioned was this assassination in an apartment building with a leg in far western Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他提到的其中一个案例就是乌克兰远西部发生的一起公寓大楼暗杀事件。

sentences.en: And this one immediately jumped out at me because it was so unlike all the other cases that I had been researching.
sentences.zh: 这个案例立即引起了我的注意，因为它与我一直在研究的所有其他案例截然不同。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Most of the assassinations that have occurred have involved high-ranking officials or military figures or journalists.
sentences.zh: 发生的大多数暗杀事件都涉及高级官员、军事人物或记者。

sentences.en: People, it's sad to say, you might expect to be targets of assassination.
sentences.zh: 遗憾地说，这些人可能是暗杀的目标。

sentences.en: This case didn't seem to fit any of those patterns.
sentences.zh: 这个案例似乎不符合任何这些模式。

sentences.en: The victim wasn't a well-known political figure.
sentences.zh: 受害者不是知名的政治人物。

sentences.en: He wasn't a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 他不是记者。

sentences.en: He was an electrician at a jail.
sentences.zh: 他是监狱里的电工。

sentences.en: He was a nobody, really.
sentences.zh: 实际上他是个无名小卒。

sentences.en: And so I was curious why anyone would want to kill him, let alone the Russians.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇为什么有人会想杀他，更不用说俄罗斯人了。

sentences.en: And yet the Ukrainian officials insisted that Russia had something to do with this.
sentences.zh: 然而乌克兰官员坚持认为俄罗斯与此有关。

sentences.en: It turned out that he was on trial and there was a hearing going on.
sentences.zh: 事实证明他正在受审，并且正在举行听证会。

sentences.en: And so I rented a car.
sentences.zh: 所以我租了一辆车。

sentences.en: I drove four hours from Kiev, the capital, to this town, Rivna, and just showed up at the courthouse.
sentences.zh: 我从首都基辅开车四个小时来到里夫纳这个小镇，然后直接出现在法院。

sentences.en: I arrived a little before anybody else got there and was in the courtroom alone.
sentences.zh: 我在其他人到达之前不久到达，独自在法庭上。

sentences.en: The courtroom is about the size of a large New York City bedroom.
sentences.zh: 法庭大约有纽约市一个大卧室那么大。

sentences.en: There's a Ukrainian flag.
sentences.zh: 一面乌克兰国旗。

sentences.en: There's a bench where a three-judge panel sits and just a few benches for spectators.
sentences.zh: 有一个三名法官组成的陪审团坐的长椅和几排旁听席。

sentences.en: There's a large steel cage where the defendants are kept.
sentences.zh: 有一个关押被告的大钢笼。

sentences.en: A steel cage.
sentences.zh: 一个钢笼。

sentences.en: A steel cage.
sentences.zh: 一个钢笼。

sentences.en: In the middle of the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 在法庭中央。

sentences.en: In the middle of the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 在法庭中央。

sentences.en: A few minutes later, the bailiffs bring this man in, Oleg, the defendant, and lock him in the cage.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，法警把这个男人、被告奥列格带进来，把他锁在笼子里。

sentences.en: And he's short in stature.
sentences.zh: 他身材矮小。

sentences.en: He's got a goatee flecked with gray hair.
sentences.zh: 他留着带有灰白头发的山羊胡。

sentences.en: He's sort of slumped.
sentences.zh: 他有点驼背。

sentences.en: He's wearing this blue track suit and a baseball cap.
sentences.zh: 他穿着这套蓝色运动服和一顶棒球帽。

sentences.en: And I walk up to Oleg and just introduce myself as a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 我走向奥列格，自我介绍说我是一名记者。

sentences.en: Through the cage.
sentences.zh: 隔着笼子。

sentences.en: Through the cage.
sentences.zh: 隔着笼子。

sentences.en: And I had expected maybe to get a few sound bites on this trip and to go home largely disappointed.
sentences.zh: 我本以为这次旅行可能会得到一些采访片段，然后带着极大的失望回家。

sentences.en: And to my great surprise.
sentences.zh: 令我大吃一惊的是。

sentences.en: Oleg just started talking and talking and talking.
sentences.zh: 奥列格开始不停地滔滔不绝地说话。

sentences.en: What did he say?
sentences.zh: 他说什么了？

sentences.en: He admitted almost immediately to having pulled the trigger at the behest of these two individuals who were his handlers.
sentences.zh: 他几乎立即承认是在作为他上级的这两个人的唆使下开枪的。

sentences.en: And then the judges walk in and were cut off.
sentences.zh: 然后法官走进来，谈话被打断了。

sentences.en: And Oleg suggests that I come back after the trial and talk to him in jail where he has all the time he needs.
sentences.zh: 奥列格建议我在审判结束后回来，去监狱里找他，在那里他有他需要的所有时间。

sentences.en: So he is very willing to tell you this story.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常愿意告诉你这个故事。

sentences.en: Eager to tell this story.
sentences.zh: 渴望讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: And so you meet Oleg in prison.
sentences.zh: 所以你在监狱里遇到了奥列格。

sentences.en: What happens there?
sentences.zh: 那里发生了什么？

sentences.en: I go to the jail after the trial.
sentences.zh: 审判结束后我去了监狱。

sentences.en: They lead me into a small room.
sentences.zh: 他们把我带到一个小房间里。

sentences.en: There's a table, there's chairs, and a small barred window.
sentences.zh: 有一张桌子、椅子和一个带铁栏杆的小窗户。

sentences.en: After a few minutes, they bring Oleg in.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，他们把奥列格带了进来。

sentences.en: And we're left alone in there.
sentences.zh: 我们在里面只剩下我们两个人。

sentences.en: I pull out my recorder and start talking to him.
sentences.zh: 我掏出录音机开始跟他交谈。

sentences.en: And how unusual is it to get this kind of access to these Russian assassins?
sentences.zh: 能接触到这些俄罗斯刺客，这种机会有多罕见？

sentences.en: The successful ones you never find.
sentences.zh: 那些成功的刺客，你永远也找不到。

sentences.en: And the unsuccessful ones usually end up dead.
sentences.zh: 而那些不成功的，通常都死掉了。

sentences.en: And so it's rare to find an unsuccessful assassin who is captured and contained in a way that allows them to be interviewed.
sentences.zh: 因此，能找到一个落网并被控制、甚至还能接受采访的失败刺客，是非常罕见的。

sentences.en: And Oleg is uniquely in that sweet spot.
sentences.zh: 而奥列格恰好处于这个绝佳的平衡点上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What does he tell you when you guys start to talk?
sentences.zh: 你们开始交谈时，他对你说了什么？

sentences.en: He started with a poem that I don't really remember.
sentences.zh: 他从一首我记不太清的诗开始。

sentences.en: He said some sort of poem and then started rattling a few things off in English.
sentences.zh: 他念了某种诗，然后开始用英语连珠炮似地说了一些事情。

sentences.en: But very early on in our conversation, he brings out this map.
sentences.zh: 但在我们对话的早期，他就拿出了这张地图。

sentences.en: This map that he had drawn on a piece of graph paper ripped out of a notebook.
sentences.zh: 这张他画在从笔记本上撕下来的方格纸上的地图。

sentences.en: The map shows downtown Moscow.
sentences.zh: 地图显示的是莫斯科市中心。

sentences.en: And he points to this little shaded square that is labeled Vienna Café.
sentences.zh: 他指着一个标有“维也纳咖啡馆”的小阴影方块。

sentences.en: And this is around the corner from the headquarters of Russia's domestic intelligence agency, the FSB, which is the successor of the KGB.
sentences.zh: 这个地方就在俄罗斯国内情报机构联邦安全局（FSB，前身是克格勃）总部的拐角处。

sentences.en: And he points to this square and said, this is where I met with my handlers.
sentences.zh: 他指着这个方块说，这就是我和联络人见面切磋的地方。

sentences.en: This is where I would meet with them.
sentences.zh: 这就是我会和他们碰头的地方。

sentences.en: In downtown Moscow, around the corner from the FSB.
sentences.zh: 在莫斯科市中心，FSB的拐角处。

sentences.en: At a coffee shop.
sentences.zh: 在一家咖啡馆里。

sentences.en: And these were the guys that gave Oleg the list of names with six targets, one of them being Ivan, who lived in the apartment in Rivna.
sentences.zh: 就是这些人给了奥列格那份包含六个目标的名单，其中一个就是住在里夫纳公寓里的伊万。

sentences.en: And so Oleg, it sounds like, is part of the Russian intelligence system.
sentences.zh: 听起来，奥列格是俄罗斯情报系统的一部分喽？

sentences.en: No, in fact.
sentences.zh: 不，事实上。

sentences.en: He was not an intelligence officer.
sentences.zh: 他不是情报人员。

sentences.en: He spent much of his life involved in various criminal pursuits.
sentences.zh: 他的一生大都在参与各种犯罪活动。

sentences.en: This is a criminal.
sentences.zh: 这是个罪犯。

sentences.en: He was involved in an extortion racket in the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 他在21世纪初参与过敲诈勒索。

sentences.en: He served two stints in jail for bribery and fraud.
sentences.zh: 他曾因行贿和诈骗两次入狱。

sentences.en: He was involved in sex trafficking.
sentences.zh: 他曾参与人口贩运。

sentences.en: This is not a good guy.
sentences.zh: 这不是个好人。

sentences.en: This is not a pleasant man.
sentences.zh: 这不是个讨人喜欢的人。

sentences.en: And at some point, he finds himself at a gun show in Moscow, where he's trying to find some kind of accessory for a weapon that he has.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他发现自己身处莫斯科的一个枪展上，试图为自己的一把武器找点配件。

sentences.en: And it's at this gun show that he meets some individuals who offer him employment.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个枪展上，他遇到了一些提供工作机会的人。

sentences.en: Say that they know some people who might be looking for somebody with his particular skills and would he like to meet him.
sentences.zh: 对方说他们认识一些可能在寻找具备他这种特殊技能的人，问他愿不愿意去见见他们。

sentences.en: And that is when he was introduced to these two individuals who became his handlers.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，他被介绍给了这两个后来成为他联络人的人。

sentences.en: And what is Oleg's understanding, after speaking with these handlers, of what his job is going to be?
sentences.zh: 在与这些联络人交谈之后，奥列格认为他的工作会是什么？

sentences.en: He's getting older.
sentences.zh: 他正在变老。

sentences.en: He is starting to think about his future.
sentences.zh: 他开始考虑自己的未来。

sentences.en: And what he really wants out of this is a pension.
sentences.zh: 他从这当中真正想要的是一份养老金。

sentences.en: I think it's a pension.
sentences.zh: 我想是一笔养老金。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Pension.
sentences.zh: 养老金。

sentences.en: He sees this as sort of his way, his entry into a government job with the Russian government that would allow him to one day retire with a pension.
sentences.zh: 他将此视为通往俄罗斯政府工作的途径、一种进入政府部门的方式，这样他有一天就能带着养老金退休。

sentences.en: So, in his mind, he can do this job.
sentences.zh: 所以，在他看来，他可以做这份工作。

sentences.en: He can carry out this task and be kind of financially set for the rest of his life.
sentences.zh: 他可以执行这项任务，并且在余生中获得某种财务保障。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And keep in mind, according to Oleg, he doesn't know that he's going to kill anybody at this point.
sentences.zh: 并且记住，根据奥列格的说法，他此时并不知道自己要去杀人。

sentences.en: He knows that he wants to get into the government in some way, and he wants to find some way to pay for his retirement.
sentences.zh: 他知道自己想以某种方式进入政府，他想找到某种支付退休金的方法。

sentences.en: But he doesn't exactly know what the task is.
sentences.zh: 但他并不确切知道任务是什么。

sentences.en: And when does he learn what the job actually entails?
sentences.zh: 那他是什么时候知道这份工作实际内容的？

sentences.en: According to Oleg, he went to Rivna to start conducting surveillance of this individual at this apartment building under the impression that that is all he was going to do.
sentences.zh: 根据奥列格的说法，他去里夫纳开始对这栋公寓楼里的这个人进行监视时，以为这就是他要做的全部。

sentences.en: He did know that a murder was going to take place.
sentences.zh: 他确实知道会发生谋杀。

sentences.en: He did know that this man was targeted for murder.
sentences.zh: 他确实知道这个人是谋杀的目标。

sentences.en: But he insists, and he insists this to me, and he tells this to the prosecutors and the judges in the case,
sentences.zh: 但他坚称——他对我是这么坚称的，他也对本案的检察官和法官这么说——

sentences.en: and he claims it was a great surprise to him that he was then asked to carry out the murder himself.
sentences.zh: 他声称，后来被要求自己去执行谋杀让他感到非常意外。

sentences.en: So, when you leave this interview, what have you learned about this list?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你结束这次采访时，你对这份名单有了什么了解？

sentences.en: What did he tell you about why they were being targeted by the Russian government?
sentences.zh: 他有没有告诉你，他们为什么会成为俄罗斯政府的目标？

sentences.en: He knows very little other than he suspects that this is revenge for something.
sentences.zh: 他知之甚少，只怀疑这是某种报复。

sentences.en: But he does give me the list, which allows me to go look into this question for myself.
sentences.zh: 但他确实把名单交给了我，这让我能够亲自去调查这个问题。

sentences.en: He gives you access to the assassination liSt.
sentences.zh: 他让你接触了暗杀名单。

sentences.en: Gives me access to the assassination list, and I sort of embark on this journey trying to figure out why.
sentences.zh: 让我接触到了暗杀名单，于是我开始踏上这段旅程，试图找出原因。

sentences.en: Why these individuals, what made them targets.
sentences.zh: 为什么是这些人，是什么让他们成了目标。

sentences.en: And how do you do that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Google is a good place to start.
sentences.zh: 谷歌是个不错的起点。

sentences.en: I take the names, and I just start Googling them.
sentences.zh: 我拿着这些名字，开始在谷歌上搜索。

sentences.en: I start asking sources that I have in Ukraine about them.
sentences.zh: 我开始向我在乌克兰的消息源打听他们。

sentences.en: Very quickly, I learned that some of them have military backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 很快，我得知他们中的一些人有军事背景。

sentences.en: But the thing that stands out as most important is that they were all connected in some way to a 2008 war between Russia and the Republic of Georgia.
sentences.zh: 但最重要、最突出的事情是，他们都以某种方式与2008年俄罗斯和格鲁吉亚共和国之间的战争有关。

sentences.en: A war that, for Russia, ended up being a very big embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 对俄罗斯来说，那场战争最终成了一件非常尴尬的事。

sentences.en: Bombings and firefights still raging, and Georgian forces in retreat.
sentences.zh: 轰炸和交火仍在肆虐，格鲁吉亚军队在撤退。

sentences.en: Russian troops have pushed their way into Georgia itself.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯军队已经打进了格鲁吉亚本土。

sentences.en: I think I vaguely recall this conflict, but what was so embarrassing about it for Russia?
sentences.zh: 我想我隐约记得这场冲突，但它对俄罗斯来说有什么尴尬的？

sentences.en: Well, firstly, Russia crushed the Georgian army in a matter of days.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，俄罗斯在几天内就粉碎了格鲁吉亚军队。

sentences.en: This was a massive superpower against a tiny little army.
sentences.zh: 这是一场超级大国对阵微小军队的战争。

sentences.en: But what Russia didn't expect was that Georgia had these sophisticated anti-aircraft systems that were just blowing Russian planes out of the sky.
sentences.zh: 但俄罗斯没有料到的是，格鲁吉亚拥有这些先进的防空系统，能直接把俄罗斯飞机从天上打下来。

sentences.en: Georgian rockets rained down on the South Ossetian capital.
sentences.zh: 格鲁吉亚的火箭弹倾泻在南奥塞梯首府。

sentences.en: Several pilots were killed, some were captured.
sentences.zh: 数名飞行员丧生，一些人被俘。

sentences.en: This became a major intelligence failure.
sentences.zh: 这成了一次重大情报失利。

sentences.en: Russia routed Georgia's army in five days.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯在五天内击溃了格鲁吉亚军队。

sentences.en: Despite its victory, Moscow worried about its shortcomings on the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 尽管取得了胜利，莫斯科还是对自己在战场上的短板感到担忧。

sentences.en: Putin was livid.
sentences.zh: 普京大发雷霆。

sentences.en: And when Russia started looking into this, they discovered that it was Ukraine that had secretly sold these weapons systems to Georgia in advance of the war.
sentences.zh: 当俄罗斯开始调查此事时，他们发现是乌克兰在战前秘密向格鲁吉亚出售了这些武器系统。

sentences.en: And this just set Putin off.
sentences.zh: 这彻底惹恼了普京。

sentences.en: He became incredibly angry and vowed to find the people that were responsible for providing Georgia these weapons.
sentences.zh: 他变得极其愤怒，发誓要找出那些负责向格鲁吉亚提供这些武器的人。

sentences.en: What he said was, we don't know who decided to deliver the equipment and weapons from Ukraine during the conflict.
sentences.zh: 他说的是，我们不知道是谁决定在冲突期间从乌克兰运送装备和武器。

sentences.en: But whoever it was, that person made a huge mistake.
sentences.zh: 但无论那是谁，那个人犯了一个大错误。

sentences.en: And so these six names on this list that Oleg has, what do we know about their involvement in this Georgian conflict?
sentences.zh: 那么奥列格拥有的这份名单上的这六个名字，我们对他们卷入这场格鲁吉亚冲突了解多少？

sentences.en: Even with my digging, we don't know a lot.
sentences.zh: 即使经过我的深挖，我们知道的也不多。

sentences.en: We know that all of them had some connection to the Georgian War.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们都与格鲁吉亚战争有某种联系。

sentences.en: But it was really hard to find anything specifically about their involvement.
sentences.zh: 但要找到任何关于他们具体参与情况的信息真的很难。

sentences.en: One I found in a government document.
sentences.zh: 我从一份政府文件中找到了一个人。

sentences.en: Several I found named in books about the war that were written by Russian authors.
sentences.zh: 我从俄罗斯作家写的关于这场战争的书籍中找到了好几个被点名的人。

sentences.en: One of the men on the list I met, and he claimed to have been in Georgia during this time, but didn't even take part in the war.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了名单上的一个人，他声称自己当时在格鲁吉亚，但甚至没有参加战争。

sentences.en: And so what is clear is that, you know, these people don't appear to have played a very big role, if any, in the fighting.
sentences.zh: 所以显而易见的是，你知道，这些人似乎并没有在战斗中发挥很大的作用（如果有的话）。

sentences.en: And there's no evidence to suggest that they had anything to do with these missile systems that shot down Russian planes.
sentences.zh: 也没有证据表明他们与击落俄罗斯战机的导弹系统有任何关系。

sentences.en: That includes Ivan Mamchor, the man who was killed.
sentences.zh: 其中包括被杀害的男子伊万·马姆丘尔。

sentences.en: It had been eight years since the war in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 格鲁吉亚战争已经过去八年了。

sentences.en: He was doing nothing that would seem to constitute a threat to Russia.
sentences.zh: 他当时做的任何事看起来都不构成对俄罗斯的威胁。

sentences.en: But for some reason, they came after him, and they killed him.
sentences.zh: 但不知为何，他们还是找上门来杀了他。

sentences.en: It sounds like, to the degree the people on this list were involved in the Georgian conflict and in embarrassing Russia, it might have been quite peripheral.
sentences.zh: 听起来，就这份名单上的人卷入格鲁吉亚冲突并让俄罗斯感到尴尬的程度而言，可能相当边缘化。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you know, the problem is, is like, we just don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，你知道，问题在于，我们根本不知道。

sentences.en: We don't know what the motivation was, why, you know, eight years after the fact, suddenly they send a leg to go start handling this problem,
sentences.zh: 我们不知道动机是什么，为什么，你知道，在事情发生八年后，他们突然派奥列格去处理这个烂摊子，

sentences.en: why they were still so burnt up about it.
sentences.zh: 为什么他们对此仍然耿耿于怀。

sentences.en: I talked to one Ukrainian intelligence officials who just described this as a bureaucratic problem.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的一位乌克兰情报官员将其形容为一个官僚主义问题。

sentences.en: Somebody discovered that a file was left open and not resolved, and somebody said about resolving it.
sentences.zh: 有人发现有一个档案被搁置而没有解决，于是有人着手去解决它。

sentences.en: Meaning like a file of Russian grievance.
sentences.zh: 意思是像一个俄罗斯怨恨档案。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In other words, there is no slight, too small, or old, because Russia doesn't forget.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，没有太小或太陈旧的轻蔑，因为俄罗斯不会忘记。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Russia will remember, the Kremlin will remember, and in a lot of cases, they come after you.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯会记住，克里姆林宫会记住，在很多情况下，他们会来找你算账。

sentences.en: If you look at Skripal, and if you look at Mamchor, and if you look at any number of people that we believe have been murdered by the Russian state,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看斯克里帕尔，如果你看看马姆丘尔，如果你看看我们认为被俄罗斯国家谋杀的任何其他人，

sentences.en: these killings, these attacks, seem to serve no geopolitical purpose.
sentences.zh: 这些谋杀和袭击似乎没有任何地缘政治目的。

sentences.en: They are individual, petty slights that the Kremlin is pursuing, that the Kremlin is seeking satisfaction for.
sentences.zh: 它们是克里姆林宫正在追寻的、正在寻求满意的个体的、琐碎的轻蔑。

sentences.en: And that's what sort of sets Russia apart from other countries.
sentences.zh: 这就是使俄罗斯与其他国家不同的地方。

sentences.en: It operates more like, you know, a mafia organization, an organized crime syndicate than it does a state.
sentences.zh: 它的运作更像是一个黑手党组织、一个有组织犯罪集团，而不是一个国家。

sentences.en: It almost often seems as if it's sort of Putin's personal animosities that are driving these attacks and driving these killings.
sentences.zh: 通常看起来，似乎正是普京个人的敌意在推动这些袭击和谋杀。

sentences.en: But the one thing that's interesting, and even perhaps more scary about this case, is that not only is the target insignificant, but the assassin is a nobody.
sentences.zh: 但有一点很有趣，关于这个案子甚至更让人害怕的是，不仅目标微不足道，刺客也是个无名小卒。

sentences.en: I think there's this assumption about Russian spies that they're the elites, they're highly trained.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对俄罗斯间谍有一种假设，认为他们是精英，受过高度训练。

sentences.en: Russia is one of the most well-funded, most populous spy services in the world.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯拥有世界上资金最充足、人口最多的间谍机构之一。

sentences.en: And yet, Oleg was a criminal.
sentences.zh: 然而，奥列格是个罪犯。

sentences.en: He was untrained.
sentences.zh: 他没有接受过训练。

sentences.en: He was not an intelligence officer, based upon everything that we know.
sentences.zh: 根据我们所了解的一切，他不是情报人员。

sentences.en: And that, to me, is probably more terrifying than anything else.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这可能比其他任何事情都更让人恐惧。

sentences.en: How many Olegs are there out there?
sentences.zh: 外面有多少个奥列格？

sentences.en: How many people are out there willing to work for the Russian government to kill people?
sentences.zh: 外面有多少人愿意为俄罗斯政府卖命去杀人？

sentences.en: How many people can be recruited to murder other people, to match with the myriad grievances that Russia possesses?
sentences.zh: 有多少人可以被招募去谋杀他人，以配合俄罗斯怀有的种种怨恨？

sentences.en: If you can recruit a kind of nobody on the street.
sentences.zh: 如果你能在街上招募到一个无名小卒。

sentences.en: Then you can recruit anybody.
sentences.zh: 那么你就可以招募任何人。

sentences.en: And it feels like the answer is, there are a lot of Olegs, and there are a lot of grievances.
sentences.zh: 感觉答案是，有很多个奥列格，也有很多的怨恨。

sentences.en: I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 我想这是真的。

sentences.en: I'm curious what will happen to Oleg in the end.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇奥列格最终会怎么样。

sentences.en: Did he end up getting that pension from Russia that he thought would kind of set him off for the rest of his life?
sentences.zh: 他最终拿到俄罗斯给他的那笔他认为能让他安度余生的养老金了吗？

sentences.en: He certainly didn't get a pension.
sentences.zh: 他当然没有拿到养老金。

sentences.en: He did get a few thousand dollars, a Mercedes van, and a dinner at a Japanese sushi chain in exchange for this murder.
sentences.zh: 为了这次谋杀，他确实得到了几千美元、一辆梅赛德斯厢式车，以及在日本寿司连锁店的一顿饭。

sentences.en: But he'll never be able to use the money or the car.
sentences.zh: 但他永远无法使用这些钱或这辆车。

sentences.en: He's sitting in a Ukrainian jail and almost certainly will be convicted and possibly spend the rest of his life in a Ukrainian prison.
sentences.zh: 他正坐在乌克兰的监狱里，几乎肯定会被定罪，并且可能在乌克兰监狱里度过余生。

sentences.en: He's holding out hope that Russia is going to help him, that perhaps he might be exchanged for a Ukrainian prisoner on the Russian side.
sentences.zh: 他还在抱有一线希望，希望俄罗斯会帮助他，希望自己或许能与俄罗斯方面的乌克兰囚犯进行交换。

sentences.en: But the Russians have shown no interest in his welfare at all.
sentences.zh: 但俄罗斯人对他的死活完全没有表现出任何兴趣。

sentences.en: By all accounts, for Russia, he's just disposable.
sentences.zh: 从各方面来看，对俄罗斯而言，他只是一次性的。

sentences.en: As one official told me,
sentences.zh: 正如一位官员对我说的那样，

sentences.en: on a disposable only patron, he's a used bullet.
sentences.zh: 对于只能用一次的主子来说，他就是一颗用过的子弹。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在App里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》App，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他事情。

sentences.en: On Sunday, the Secretary of Homeland Security, Kirstjen Nielsen, resigned amid growing frustration from President Trump
sentences.zh: 周日，在特朗普总统日益增长的不满声中，国土安全部长克尔斯滕·尼尔森辞职了

sentences.en: over the number of migrants seeking asylum at the southern border.
sentences.zh: 针对在南部边境寻求庇护的移民数量。

sentences.en: Nielsen's departure comes just days after the president dumped his nominee to run the Immigrations and Customs Enforcement Agency,
sentences.zh: 尼尔森离职的几天前，总统刚刚放弃了移民和海关执法局局长候选人的提名，

sentences.en: Ronald Vitello, because the president said he did not believe that Vitello would be tough enough on immigration.
sentences.zh: 罗纳德·维特洛，因为总统说他认为维特洛在移民问题上态度不够强硬。

sentences.en: Ron's a good man, but we're going in a tougher direction.
sentences.zh: 罗恩是个好人，但我们要朝一个更强硬的方向前进。

sentences.en: We want to go in a tougher direction.
sentences.zh: 我们想要朝一个更强硬的方向前进。

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 并且

sentences.en: Over the weekend, Israel's Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, pledged that if re-elected,
sentences.zh: 周末期间，以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡承诺，如果再次当选，

sentences.en: he would annex Jewish settlements in the West Bank, imposing Israeli authority over the highly disputed territory.
sentences.zh: 他将吞并约旦河西岸的犹太人定居点，对这片争议极大的领土实施以色列管辖。

sentences.en: The pledge, which will appeal to conservative voters ahead of Tuesday's election, would all but end the possibility of a two-state peace deal with Palestinians,
sentences.zh: 这一承诺将吸引周二大选前的保守派选民，这也几乎彻底断绝了与巴勒斯坦人达成两国和平协议的可能性，

sentences.en: since Palestinians consider the West Bank the heart of a future state.
sentences.zh: 因为巴勒斯坦人将约旦河西岸视为未来国家的核心。

sentences.en: Polls show that the election for prime minister remains close, but Netanyahu's party is expected to have a better chance than his rival of forming a ruling coalition.
sentences.zh: 民调显示，总理选举依然胶着，但预计内塔尼亚胡的政党比其竞争对手更有机会组建执政联盟。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》。我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目中，我们将为假期招待客人做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的妙招。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是遮光睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们喝到断片才睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》App或你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
